kurz: Cold dulls sweetness and aroma, warmth strengthens both: food served cold therefore needs stronger seasoning.
bild_im_kopf: Like a voice in fog: in the cold the same message arrives only muffled.
was_passiert: Part of the signal chain for sweetness works much harder when warm. Aroma compounds are volatile: warm food releases far more of them than cold. Very hot food, on the other hand, masks fine nuances because the heat itself takes centre stage.
warum_wichtig: Explains why potato salad tastes bland the next day, ice cream base tastes too sweet when warm and a hot soup suddenly seems oversalted once it cools.
faustregeln: Taste food served cold while cold and season it more strongly.
Don't taste soups and sauces boiling hot: let a spoonful cool briefly.
Don't serve cheese and red wine ice-cold, or their aroma stays silent.

stellschrauben.wirkung: Warmer tastes sweeter and smells stronger, colder more muted
